Our crucial research equipment is for automated synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, analytics for biomolecules and other metabolites, and fermentation and downstream processes. Additionally, we house multiple 2L industry-standard bioreactors capable of accommodating both aerobic and anaerobic conditions, providing a versatile platform for advanced research and experimentation. For pilot-scale production, we have on-site fermentors ranging from 20L to 100L. Downs

notes:

notes:

Innovators can use ZAP’s expertise, facilities and available space to test and scale up their processes.

name: Lonza Biologics Portsmouth
legacy: State: NH. Part of Lonza's global biologics CDMO network. Capacity ~20,000 L mammalian.
notes: Lonza's Portsmouth site is a large-scale biologics CDMO offering mammalian cell culture manufacturing in stirred-tank bioreactors up to 20,000 L. The facility specialises in monoclonal antibody and recombinant protein production under full FDA and EMA GMP compliance.

name: Lonza Biologics Hopkinton
legacy: State: MA. Historical Millipore site, integrated into Lonza portfolio.
notes: Lonza's Hopkinton facility provides mammalian and microbial contract manufacturing services for biopharmaceuticals. The site handles both clinical and commercial production of proteins and antibodies, with integrated downstream and fill-finish capabilities.

name: Lonza Biologics Vacaville
legacy: State: CA. Former Genentech Vacaville site, purchased by Lonza in 2011.
notes: One of the largest biologics contract manufacturing sites in the world, the Vacaville facility runs stainless-steel stirred-tank bioreactors at commercial scale for monoclonal antibodies and other large-molecule therapeutics. Originally built by Genentech and acquired by Lonza.

name: WuXi Biologics (Cranbury)
legacy: State: NJ. WuXi Biologics' primary US commercial-scale facility.
notes: WuXi Biologics' US commercial manufacturing site in New Jersey supports late-phase clinical and commercial production of biologics for global biotech and pharma clients. The facility uses single-use bioreactors and integrated purification suites.

name: WuXi Biologics (Worcester)
legacy: State: MA. Formerly part of Sanofi Genzyme's Framingham/Allston campus network.
notes: WuXi Biologics' Worcester facility provides early- to late-phase biologics contract manufacturing services. The site was established via acquisition of Sanofi's biologics manufacturing campus and focuses on mammalian cell culture drug substance production.

name: Catalent Biologics Bloomington
capacity: Up to 4 × 4,000 L single-use bioreactors + fill-finish
legacy: Site acquired from Eli Lilly in 2018; significantly expanded for biologics and gene therapy manufacturing.
notes: One of Catalent's largest biologics campuses; strong in gene therapy fill-finish.

name: Catalent Biologics Madison
legacy: State: WI. Drug product manufacturing focus; complements Bloomington drug substance site.
notes: Catalent's Madison site specialises in formulation development and drug product manufacturing for biologics, including liquid and lyophilised injectables. The facility is a key hub for late-phase clinical and commercial drug product supply.

name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies (RTP)
legacy: State: NC. Extensive expansion underway 2023–2026 to add large-scale mRNA and gene therapy capacity.
notes: Fujifilm Diosynth's Research Triangle Park campus is a flagship biologics CDMO offering mammalian and microbial manufacturing. The site provides integrated services from cell line development through commercial supply, with a strong gene therapy capability added via the acquisition of Hitachi Chemical's biologics division.

name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies (College Station)
legacy: State: TX. DragonFly facility; ~130,000 sq ft. Designed for rapid scale-up and flexible manufacturing.
notes: Fujifilm Diosynth's College Station facility is one of the world's largest single-use biopharmaceutical manufacturing sites. The facility, known as 'DragonFly', houses numerous 2,000 L single-use bioreactors for mammalian cell culture and was designed for flexible, high-speed commercial biologics production.

name: Boehringer Ingelheim BioXcellence (St. Joseph)
legacy: State: MO. World's largest single-site biopharmaceutical CDMO by bioreactor volume.
notes: Boehringer Ingelheim's St. Joseph site is one of North America's premier biologics contract manufacturers. Operating under the BioXcellence brand, the site offers large-scale mammalian and microbial biopharmaceutical manufacturing services with stainless-steel bioreactors from 10 L to 240,000 L.

name: Boehringer Ingelheim BioXcellence (Fremont)
legacy: State: CA. Former Roche Diagnostics site; expanded under Boehringer Ingelheim ownership.
notes: Boehringer Ingelheim's Fremont facility provides mammalian and microbial contract manufacturing for clinical and commercial biopharmaceuticals. The site was acquired from Roche/Genentech and expanded to support the growing BioXcellence CDMO portfolio.

name: AGC Biologics (Seattle)
legacy: State: WA (Bothell). Formerly CMC Biologics; acquired by AGC Inc. (Asahi Glass). Includes API and drug product suites.
notes: AGC Biologics' Seattle-area campus in Bothell is a full-service biologics CDMO providing mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation services from process development through commercial manufacturing. The site is one of AGC Biologics' primary North American facilities.

name: AGC Biologics (Boulder)
legacy: State: CO. Focus on clinical-phase biologics and process development services.
notes: AGC Biologics' Boulder facility specialises in process development and clinical-scale manufacturing of biologics and high-potency APIs. The site offers flexible single-use and stainless-steel bioreactor capacity for early-phase biologics programs.

name: KBI BioPharma (Durham)
legacy: State: NC. Subsidiary of JSR Corporation (Japan). Integrated drug substance to drug product CDMO.
notes: KBI BioPharma's Durham site is a biologics CDMO providing integrated drug substance and drug product services. The facility offers mammalian cell culture manufacturing, downstream processing, and aseptic fill-finish for clinical and commercial programs.

name: KBI BioPharma (Rockville)
legacy: State: MD. Process development and analytical hub complementing Durham manufacturing campus.
notes: KBI BioPharma's Maryland site provides biologics process development and analytical testing services. The site offers structural characterisation, forced degradation studies, and accelerated stability testing to support IND and BLA submissions.

name: Emergent BioSolutions (Bayview)
legacy: State: MD. Key US government BARDA contract manufacturing facility for biodefense products.
notes: Emergent BioSolutions' Baltimore Bayview campus is a major biologics and vaccine contract manufacturer. The site produces anthrax vaccine (BioThrax), smallpox vaccine, and has significant CDMO capacity for government and commercial clients. The facility attracted scrutiny during COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing in 2021.

name: Emergent BioSolutions (Lansing)
legacy: State: MI. Specialises in bacterial biopharmaceuticals and immunotherapy products.
notes: Emergent BioSolutions' Lansing facility manufactures BCG-based immunotherapies and other biological products. The site operates under government supply contracts and commercial agreements, with capabilities in bacterial fermentation and drug substance production.

name: National Resilience (Alachua)
legacy: State: FL. Resilience acquired multiple gene therapy CDMOs to build a national manufacturing network.
notes: National Resilience's Alachua facility provides contract manufacturing for viral vectors and advanced gene therapies. The site, formerly part of the Florida biomanufacturing ecosystem, offers GMP-grade AAV, lentiviral vector, and oncolytic virus production.

name: National Resilience (Marlborough)
legacy: State: MA. Former Sanofi Genzyme Allston campus; repurposed for mRNA and cell therapy manufacturing.
notes: National Resilience's Marlborough campus was formerly the Sanofi/Genzyme Allston biologics manufacturing site. Acquired by Resilience, it now operates as an advanced manufacturing hub for complex biologics and mRNA therapeutics, leveraging the infrastructure of one of New England's largest biomanufacturing facilities.

name: Cytovance Biologics
legacy: State: OK. Founded 2004 at OMRF campus. Focus on Phase I–III clinical manufacturing.
notes: Cytovance Biologics is a full-service CDMO based at the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation campus, offering mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation manufacturing for clinical-stage biologics. The company provides end-to-end services including cell line development, process development, and GMP production.

name: Goodwin Biotechnology
legacy: State: FL. Niche specialist in insect cell expression and VLP manufacturing.
notes: Goodwin Biotechnology is a specialist CDMO offering mammalian and insect cell culture manufacturing services. The company is particularly well-known for baculovirus-insect cell expression for VLP, subunit vaccine, and recombinant protein production at clinical scale.

name: Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services
legacy: State: CA. Subsidiary of Ajinomoto Co. (Japan). Formerly Althea Technologies, rebranded 2014.
notes: Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services (formerly Althea Technologies) is a San Diego-based CDMO specialising in microbial fermentation, mammalian cell culture, and drug product manufacturing. The facility offers GMP production from lab scale to commercial volumes, with particular strength in E. coli refolding and inclusion body processing.

name: ElevateBio BaseCamp
legacy: State: MA. Founded 2017; significant investment from GV, F-Prime, Vida Ventures.
notes: ElevateBio's BaseCamp is an integrated cell and gene therapy development and manufacturing facility. The platform supports AAV, lentiviral vector, and ex vivo cell therapy manufacturing from research scale through clinical GMP production. ElevateBio combines technology development with CDMO services.

name: Andelyn Biosciences
legacy: State: OH. Spun out of Nationwide Children's Hospital 2021. Manufactured AveXis/Novartis Zolgensma AAV9.
notes: Andelyn Biosciences (formerly Nationwide Children's Hospital's gene therapy manufacturing arm) is a leading viral vector CDMO. The company manufactures AAV gene therapies at clinical and commercial scale and has powered multiple FDA-approved gene therapy products including Zolgensma.

name: Forge Biologics
legacy: State: OH (Grove City). Founded 2019; purpose-built Giga-scale Manufacturing Facility (GMF) opened 2022.
notes: Forge Biologics is a gene therapy CDMO dedicated to AAV manufacturing. The company operates its Giga-scale Manufacturing Facility (GMF), designed to produce clinical and commercial AAV at unprecedented scale and cost-efficiency, supporting the advancement of rare disease gene therapies.

name: Abzena (Bristol PA)
legacy: State: NJ. Formerly part of TCRS and PolyTherics; merged to form Abzena. Strong ADC and bioconjugation capability.
notes: Abzena's US facilities provide integrated biologics and bioconjugate manufacturing services, with a focus on antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), conjugation chemistry, and mammalian cell culture. The company offers end-to-end services from antibody development through clinical GMP manufacturing.

name: Rentschler Biopharma (Milford)
legacy: State: MA. German-origin family-owned CDMO; US site opened 2020 to serve North American clients.
notes: Rentschler Biopharma's US site in Milford, Massachusetts provides mammalian cell culture manufacturing services for clinical and commercial biologics. The site was established to bring European CDMO capabilities to the American market, offering single-use and stainless-steel bioreactor capacity.

name: Therapure Biopharma
legacy: Province: ON. Formerly Bayer Biologicals facility, converted to CDMO operations. Canada's largest biologics CMO.
notes: Therapure Biopharma is Canada's leading biologics CDMO, providing mammalian cell culture, plasma protein manufacturing, and drug product services. The Mississauga facility was originally built for Bayer's pharmaceutical operations and is now a full-service CDMO supporting both domestic and international clients.

name: BioVectra
legacy: Province: PEI. Acquired by Thermo Fisher Scientific in 2021.
notes: BioVectra is a Canadian CDMO specialising in highly potent APIs, oligonucleotides, and biological APIs. Based in Prince Edward Island, the company operates GMP manufacturing facilities for complex synthetic and biologically derived active pharmaceutical ingredients serving global biotech and pharma companies.

name: Oxford Biomedica Solutions
legacy: State: MA. Oxford Biomedica US site; complements UK Harrow Court manufacturing campus.
notes: Oxford Biomedica Solutions (formerly Homology Medicines' manufacturing site) is a viral vector CDMO providing GMP lentiviral and AAV manufacturing services. The site leverages Oxford Biomedica's LentiVector platform and supports clinical and commercial cell and gene therapy programs.

name: Amgen Thousand Oaks
legacy: State: CA. Founded 1980; first site and global HQ. Employs ~6,000 at this campus.
notes: Amgen's world headquarters and original manufacturing campus in Thousand Oaks has been a cornerstone of the US biopharmaceutical industry since the company's founding in 1980. The site produces multiple blockbuster biologics including Enbrel, Aranesp, and Prolia, and houses Amgen's principal R&D operations.

name: Amgen West Greenwich
legacy: State: RI. Among world's largest single biologics sites by bioreactor volume. Key Enbrel supply site.
notes: Amgen's Rhode Island campus is one of the world's largest biologics manufacturing facilities, housing commercial-scale mammalian cell culture bioreactors. The site produces key Amgen products including Enbrel (etanercept) at scale, with stainless-steel bioreactors exceeding 75,000 L total installed capacity.

name: Genentech (South San Francisco)
legacy: State: CA. Founded 1976 by Boyer & Swanson; part of Roche since 2009. Historic birthplace of biotech manufacturing.
notes: Genentech's South San Francisco headquarters is where the modern biopharmaceutical industry began. The site houses research, development, and manufacturing operations for Genentech/Roche products. It is the birthplace of recombinant DNA technology in industry and produced the first FDA-approved biotech drug (human insulin, 1982).

name: Genentech Vacaville
legacy: State: CA. ~100,000 L total installed bioreactor capacity. A portion leased/sold to Lonza CDMO operations.
notes: Genentech's Vacaville manufacturing site is a large-scale commercial biologics facility dedicated to producing Roche/Genentech medicines. The campus houses multiple manufacturing suites with 25,000 L stainless-steel bioreactors. Part of the site has been converted to Lonza CDMO operations.

name: Pfizer Andover Biologics
legacy: State: MA. Former Wyeth Pharmaceuticals site; acquired by Pfizer in 2009. Key US biologics hub.
notes: Pfizer's Andover biologics campus is a major commercial manufacturing hub for Pfizer's biopharmaceutical portfolio. The site houses mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation capabilities, producing key biologics including biosimilars and established biologic medicines.

name: AbbVie Biologics (North Chicago)
legacy: State: IL. Formerly Abbott Laboratories; spun off as AbbVie 2013. Humira production hub.
notes: AbbVie's North Chicago campus is the global headquarters and primary manufacturing site for AbbVie's biologics portfolio, including Humira (adalimumab), the world's best-selling biologic drug for over a decade. The site employs a large-scale mammalian cell culture platform.

name: Bristol-Myers Squibb Devens
legacy: State: MA. Opened 2019. $750M investment; fully single-use technology. Produces Opdivo and Orencia.
notes: Bristol-Myers Squibb's Devens facility is a state-of-the-art biologics manufacturing site built to produce Opdivo (nivolumab) and other immuno-oncology biologics at commercial scale. Opened in 2019, the facility uses single-use bioreactor technology throughout, making it one of the most modern large-scale biologics plants in the world.

name: AstraZeneca / MedImmune (Gaithersburg)
legacy: State: MD. MedImmune acquired by AstraZeneca 2007. Historically known for FluMist and Synagis manufacture.
notes: AstraZeneca's Gaithersburg campus, formerly MedImmune headquarters, is a major biologics R&D and manufacturing site. The facility produces respiratory syncytial virus vaccines (Synagis/palivizumab) and other biologics, and houses AstraZeneca's US biological research and early manufacturing operations.

name: Merck & Co. (West Point)
legacy: State: PA. ~10,000 employees; over 100-year history. Principal US site for Gardasil and Keytruda manufacturing.
notes: Merck's West Point facility is the company's largest US manufacturing campus, producing vaccines (including Gardasil, varicella), biologics, and small-molecule drugs. The site is a historic Merck manufacturing hub with over 100 years of pharmaceutical production and one of the world's largest vaccine manufacturing sites.

name: Biogen (Research Triangle Park)
legacy: State: NC. Key Biogen manufacturing hub for multiple sclerosis portfolio. Also produces Spinraza (nusinersen).
notes: Biogen's RTP campus is the company's primary US commercial biologics manufacturing site, producing multiple sclerosis therapies including Avonex (interferon beta-1a) and Tysabri (natalizumab). The site operates large-scale CHO mammalian cell culture and downstream processing facilities.

name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (Rensselaer)
legacy: State: NY. Large expansion for Dupixent (dupilumab) production ongoing. Also Limerick, Ireland site for global supply.
notes: Regeneron's Rensselaer manufacturing campus is the company's commercial biologics production hub. The site manufactures key products including Dupixent (dupilumab) and Eylea (aflibercept) using Regeneron's proprietary CHO-based manufacturing platform with large-scale stainless-steel and single-use bioreactors.

name: Novo Nordisk (Clayton)
legacy: State: NC. Multi-billion dollar expansion underway 2022–2025 to increase semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) supply.
notes: Novo Nordisk's Clayton facility is one of the company's primary US manufacturing sites, producing insulin and GLP-1 receptor agonist therapies. The site has undergone massive expansion to meet demand for semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy). It combines fermentation-based API production with drug product fill-finish.

name: Moderna (Norwood)
legacy: State: MA. Norwood manufacturing site is ~200,000 sq ft; key COVID-19 vaccine supply site from 2021.
notes: Moderna's primary US manufacturing facility for mRNA medicines and vaccines is located in Norwood, Massachusetts. The site produces mRNA drug substance and lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulated drug product, and was central to COVID-19 mRNA vaccine supply under Operation Warp Speed.

name: CSL Behring (Kankakee)
legacy: State: IL. CSL Behring global HQ is in King of Prussia, PA. Key plasma-derived protein manufacturing campus.
notes: CSL Behring's Kankakee facility is a large-scale plasma protein manufacturing site producing coagulation factors, immunoglobulins, and albumin from donor plasma. The site is part of CSL's global plasma manufacturing network and operates under full FDA and international GMP standards.

name: Eli Lilly (Indianapolis)
legacy: State: IN. Founded 1876; historic site of world's first commercial recombinant insulin (Humulin, 1982).
notes: Eli Lilly's Indianapolis headquarters campus houses manufacturing, R&D, and global operations. The site has been involved in biologics production since the first commercial recombinant insulin (Humulin) produced using E. coli fermentation technology in 1982. Current manufacturing supports diabetes, immunology, and oncology biologics.

name: Amgen Puerto Rico
legacy: Territory: PR. One of three major Amgen commercial manufacturing sites alongside Thousand Oaks and West Greenwich.
notes: Amgen's Puerto Rico manufacturing facility in Juncos is a major commercial biologics production site serving global markets. The facility produces drug substance and drug product for several key Amgen medicines and is a vital part of Amgen's global supply chain.

name: Grifols (Los Angeles)
legacy: State: CA. Grifols (Spain-based) acquired Talecris Biotherapeutics (formerly Bayer Biologics plasma) in 2011.
notes: Grifols' Los Angeles manufacturing facility is one of the company's primary North American plasma protein manufacturing sites. The facility produces immunoglobulins, albumin, and coagulation factors from human plasma using large-scale fractionation and chromatographic purification.

name: BioMarin (Novato)
legacy: State: CA. Focus on ultra-rare enzyme replacement therapies. Also has manufacturing in San Rafael, CA.
notes: BioMarin's Novato headquarters includes manufacturing operations for rare disease enzyme replacement therapies. The site produces Naglazyme (galsulfase), Aldurazyme (laronidase), and other biologically derived enzyme therapies using mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation.

name: Sanofi Genzyme (Framingham / Allston)
legacy: State: MA. Genzyme founded 1981 in Cambridge, acquired by Sanofi 2011. Allston campus partially divested to CDMOs.
notes: Sanofi Genzyme's Massachusetts manufacturing network (historically Framingham and Allston) produced rare disease biologics including Cerezyme (imiglucerase) and Myozyme (alglucosidase alfa). The Allston campus was a flagship biologics site until portions were sold to Resilience and WuXi Biologics.

name: NC State BTEC
legacy: State: NC. Opened 2007; ~65,000 sq ft; serves as training facility and pilot production resource. Affiliated with NIIMBL.
notes: The Biomanufacturing Training and Education Center (BTEC) at NC State University is a unique facility combining GMP-quality training with pilot-scale biopharmaceutical manufacturing. BTEC offers mammalian cell culture, microbial fermentation, and downstream processing at 200 L pilot scale, training the next generation of biomanufacturing professionals.

name: NIIMBL (National Institute for Innovation in Manufacturing Biopharmaceuticals)
legacy: State: DE. NIST Manufacturing USA institute. Network of 150+ member organisations across academia, industry, government.
notes: NIIMBL is a public-private partnership and national biopharmaceutical manufacturing institute funded by NIST and industry members. Based at the University of Delaware, NIIMBL coordinates research, workforce development, and technology advancement across a network of academic, government, and industry partners to modernise US biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

name: Center for Breakthrough Medicines (CBM)
legacy: State: PA. Over 700,000 sq ft; one of the largest cell & gene therapy manufacturing facilities globally.
notes: The Center for Breakthrough Medicines is one of the world's largest cell and gene therapy CDMOs. The facility provides integrated development and manufacturing services for viral vectors, T-cell therapies, and stem cell products, with state-of-the-art cleanrooms and multiple GMP suites designed for clinical and commercial cell/gene therapy programs.

name: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center Bioproduction Facility
owner: Walter Reed National Military Medical Center Bioproduction Facility
legacy: State: MD. Government/DoD facility. Supports BARDA and DARPA biodefense manufacturing programs.
notes: The Walter Reed Army Institute of Research and associated biodefense manufacturing capabilities support the development and pilot-scale production of vaccines and biologics for military and public health applications. The site collaborates with BARDA and government partners on biodefense countermeasures.

name: MIT Koch Institute (Pilot Scale Biomanufacturing)
legacy: State: MA. Academic pilot facility; Koch Institute opened 2011. Affiliated with MIT's cancer research program.
notes: MIT's Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research includes pilot-scale biomanufacturing capabilities supporting academic and startup translation of cell therapies, nanoparticle drug delivery, and novel biologics. The institute bridges discovery research and clinical-stage biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

name: Institut Armand-Frappier (IAF) – INRS
legacy: Province: QC. Public research institute affiliated with INRS (Institut national de la recherche scientifique).
notes: The Institut Armand-Frappier (IAF) at INRS is Canada's leading public bioprocessing research and pilot manufacturing centre. The facility offers pilot-scale fermentation, mammalian cell culture, and vaccine production capabilities to support academic research and industry scale-up. IAF has a long history in infectious disease research and biosafety level 2 and 3 manufacturing.

name: Vaccine and Infectious Disease Organization (VIDO)
legacy: Province: SK. Developed COVID-19 vaccine candidates. Only CL3 large-animal facility in North America.
notes: VIDO at the University of Saskatchewan is a world-leading infectious disease research and vaccine development facility with pilot GMP manufacturing capabilities. The centre develops vaccines for both human and animal health, and houses the only Containment Level 3 (CL3) large animal research facility in North America.

name: ImClone Systems (Branchburg) – CLOSED
legacy: State: NJ. Closed/restructured post-Lilly acquisition (2008). Site produced Erbitux. Historic early mAb manufacturer. [CLOSED]
notes: ImClone Systems' Branchburg facility was a pioneer in mammalian cell culture manufacturing for monoclonal antibodies, most notably Erbitux (cetuximab). After ImClone's acquisition by Eli Lilly in 2008, the site continued production before being integrated into Eli Lilly's manufacturing network and eventually restructured.

name: MedImmune (Mountain View) – CLOSED
legacy: State: CA. Closed after AstraZeneca/MedImmune consolidation ~2010. Site redeveloped for other biotech tenants. [CLOSED]
notes: MedImmune's Mountain View facility was a biologics R&D and manufacturing site primarily associated with influenza vaccine and antibody development. After AstraZeneca's acquisition of MedImmune in 2007, site activities were gradually consolidated to the Gaithersburg, Maryland campus and the Mountain View site was closed.

name: Emergent BioSolutions (Baltimore) – COVID Waste Incident
legacy: State: MD. Production halted April–July 2021 after FDA Form 483 findings. ~15M J&J doses cross-contaminated and destroyed. [CLOSED]
notes: In 2021, Emergent BioSolutions' Bayview Baltimore facility made international headlines after a manufacturing error cross-contaminated approximately 15 million doses of Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine with AstraZeneca vaccine material. The FDA halted production at the facility for several months while deficiencies were remediated. The site resumed operations after FDA reinspection.

name: GlycoFi (Lebanon) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: NH. Acquired by Merck 2006 for $400M. GlycoFi's YeastGlyco platform enabled human-like N-glycan engineering in yeast. [CLOSED]
notes: GlycoFi was a biopharmaceutical company that pioneered glycoengineering in yeast (Pichia pastoris) for the production of human-type glycoproteins. The company's Lebanon, NH facility focused on pilot-scale manufacturing of humanised glycoproteins. GlycoFi was acquired by Merck & Co. in 2006 and the site was integrated into Merck's research network.

name: Dohmen Life Science Services – CLOSED
legacy: State: WI. Ceased biologics manufacturing operations; assets divested. Dohmen retained pharmacy benefit management operations. [CLOSED]
notes: Dohmen Life Science Services operated a biologics CDMO and repackaging operation in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The company provided contract biologics manufacturing and distribution services before ceasing operations. The closure reflected consolidation pressures in the mid-size CDMO market.

name: AVI BioPharma (Bothell) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: WA. Rebranded as Sarepta Therapeutics 2012; manufacturing shifted to CMOs. Golodirsen and Eteplirsen developed here. [CLOSED]
notes: AVI BioPharma (later Sarepta Therapeutics) pioneered antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) manufacturing for rare genetic diseases including Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The Bothell facility was a key early site for GMP oligonucleotide synthesis before the company relocated manufacturing. Sarepta Therapeutics now operates from Cambridge, MA with manufacturing outsourced to CDMOs.

name: Neose Technologies (Horsham) – CLOSED
legacy: State: PA. Acquired by ratiopharm/Novo Nordisk; GlycoPEGylation technology incorporated into Novo's protein engineering platform. [CLOSED]
notes: Neose Technologies developed GlycoPEGylation technology for extending the half-life of biologic drugs through enzymatic conjugation of PEG to glycoprotein carbohydrate chains. The company's Horsham facility conducted R&D and pilot manufacturing before the company was acquired by BioGeneriX / ratiopharm and subsequently Novo Nordisk.

name: Transkaryotic Therapies (Cambridge) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: MA. Acquired by Shire 2005 for $1.6B. Replagal continued by Shire/Takeda; site eventually consolidated. [CLOSED]
notes: Transkaryotic Therapies (TKT) was a pioneer in gene-activated manufacturing and enzyme replacement therapy for rare diseases. TKT's Cambridge facility developed Replagal (agalsidase alfa) for Fabry disease. The company was acquired by Shire Pharmaceuticals in 2005, and the site was subsequently integrated into Shire's rare disease manufacturing network.

name: Recipharm Durham
legacy: State: NC. Swedish-headquartered CDMO; Durham site focuses on parenteral biologics drug product.
notes: Recipharm's Durham facility provides drug product fill-finish and biologics manufacturing services. The site offers aseptic liquid filling, lyophilisation, and parenteral drug product manufacturing for clinical and commercial biologics programs. Recipharm is a Swedish-headquartered global CDMO.

name: Ology Biosciences
legacy: State: MD. Focus on government biodefense contracts. Formerly DPT Biologics; rebranded after acquisition.
notes: Ology Biosciences (formerly DPT Biologics) is a CDMO specialising in vaccines, biologics, and drug products for US government and commercial clients. The company operates under BARDA and DoD contracts and is a key domestic biomanufacturing partner for US national security medical countermeasures.

name: Waisman Biomanufacturing
legacy: State: WI. University-affiliated non-profit CDMO. Low-cost GMP manufacturing for academic investigators with NIH funding.
notes: Waisman Biomanufacturing at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a non-profit GMP manufacturing facility providing cell and gene therapy and biologics production services to academic investigators and small biotech companies. The facility specialises in clinical-scale manufacturing for investigator-sponsored IND trials.

name: Ginkgo Bioworks (Boston)
legacy: State: MA. Public company (NYSE: DNA). Operates Foundry platform; biosecurity and agriculture verticals also active.
notes: Ginkgo Bioworks is a synthetic biology platform company that also operates as a CDMO for fermentation-based biologics, enzymes, and biosynthetic compounds. The company's Boston Foundry combines high-throughput genetic design automation with pilot and commercial fermentation scale-up services for its partner ecosystem.

name: Pfizer (McPherson)
legacy: State: KS. High-volume parenteral drug product site. One of Pfizer's largest US fill-finish facilities.
notes: Pfizer's McPherson, Kansas facility is a large sterile injectable and biologics drug product manufacturing site. The campus produces parenteral medicines at commercial scale and is one of Pfizer's key North American drug product sites supplying both the US and global markets.

name: Takeda (Cambridge/Lexington)
legacy: State: MA. Formerly Shire Pharmaceuticals; Takeda acquired Shire 2019 for $62B. Key rare disease biologics hub.
notes: Takeda's US biologics operations, consolidated after the acquisition of Shire in 2019, span Cambridge and Lexington, Massachusetts. The sites produce rare disease biologics including plasma-derived therapies (haemophilia factors) and recombinant enzyme replacement therapies for lysosomal storage disorders.

name: Gilead Sciences / Kite Pharma (Santa Monica)
legacy: State: CA. Kite Pharma acquired by Gilead 2017 for $11.9B. Yescarta was the first FDA-approved CAR-T for large B-cell lymphoma.
notes: Gilead Sciences (via Kite Pharma, acquired 2017) operates cell therapy manufacturing facilities in the Los Angeles area for its CAR-T products Yescarta (axicabtagene ciloleucel) and Tecartus (brexucabtagene autoleucel). The Santa Monica facility is Kite's primary commercial cell therapy manufacturing site.

name: Sanofi (Swiftwater)
legacy: State: PA. Major US flu vaccine supply site. Pandemic surge capacity supported by US BARDA contracts. Originally Connaught Labs (PA).
notes: Sanofi's Swiftwater facility in Pennsylvania is one of the world's largest influenza vaccine manufacturing sites. The campus produces Fluzone, Flublok, and other seasonal and pandemic influenza vaccines at massive scale using egg-based and cell culture processes. The site has strategic importance for US pandemic preparedness.

name: Wyeth Pearl River (Vaccines) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: NY. Wyeth acquired by Pfizer 2009 for $68B. Pearl River site historic for Prevnar and RotaTeq vaccine development. [CLOSED]
notes: Wyeth's Pearl River facility was a major US vaccine and biologics manufacturing site, producing Prevnar (pneumococcal conjugate vaccine) and other biologics. After Pfizer's acquisition of Wyeth in 2009, the site was evaluated for integration into Pfizer's network. Some operations continued under Pfizer while other lines were decommissioned.

name: Immunex (Seattle) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: WA. Founded 1981; pioneered Enbrel (etanercept). Acquired by Amgen 2002 for $16B. Site eventually closed by Amgen. [CLOSED]
notes: Immunex was a Seattle-based pioneer in cytokine biology and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. The company discovered and developed Enbrel (etanercept), which became one of the world's best-selling drugs. Immunex was acquired by Amgen in 2002 for $16 billion and its Seattle manufacturing and research operations were gradually folded into Amgen's network.

name: Covance Biologics (Mooresville) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: NC. Divested from Covance/LabCorp; biologics CDMO business transitioned to other operators. [CLOSED]
notes: Covance Biologics operated a CDMO biologics manufacturing facility in North Carolina, providing contract mammalian cell culture and protein purification services. Covance (a LabCorp company) subsequently divested its biologics manufacturing operations, and the site was acquired and rebranded.

name: Albany Molecular Research (AMRI) – CLOSED/ACQUIRED
legacy: State: NY. Rebranded as Curia Global (2021) after multiple acquisitions and mergers under private equity. [CLOSED]
notes: Albany Molecular Research Inc. (AMRI) operated a CDMO providing biologics and small-molecule contract manufacturing services from its Albany, NY headquarters. AMRI was acquired by Bridgepoint and subsequently merged into the global CDMO Curia Global (formerly Albany Molecular Research), which rebranded in 2021.

name: Lonza Visp
legacy: Founded 1897 as an electrochemical plant. Pivoted to biopharmaceutical CDMO services in the 1990s; now one of the world's largest CDMO sites.
notes: Flagship Lonza CDMO campus; multiple biologics suites.

name: Samsung Biologics Incheon
legacy: Founded 2011; built the world's largest single-site biologics manufacturing campus. Listed on KRX in 2016.
notes: Plants 1–4 operational; Plant 5 under construction.

name: WuXi Biologics Wuxi
legacy: Founded 2010 as part of the WuXi AppTec group. Rapid expansion to become a top-3 global biologics CDMO.
notes: Headquarters site; additional facilities in Ireland and the US.

name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies Billingham
legacy: Originated as ICI Biologicals (1980s); became Diosynth after multiple acquisitions; acquired by Fujifilm in 2011.
notes: Primary UK site; sister sites in Durham NC (US) and Hillerød (Denmark).

name: Rentschler Biopharma Laupheim
legacy: Family-owned company founded 1927 as a pharmaceutical manufacturer. Pivoted fully to CDMO biologics services in the 2000s.
notes: Fully independent, family-owned CDMO — rare at commercial scale.

name: Boehringer Ingelheim BioXcellence Biberach
capacity: >1,000,000 L total bioreactor volume (largest single-site mammalian CDMO)
legacy: Boehringer Ingelheim's biologics division started in the 1980s. BioXcellence launched as commercial CDMO brand in 2019.
notes: Claims the world's largest mammalian cell culture CDMO capacity at a single site.

name: Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services Olean
legacy: Site originated as Pfizer's fermentation facility; acquired by Ajinomoto in 2010 to expand their bio-pharma services division.
notes: Strong heritage in fermentation-derived small molecules and amino acids.

name: Novasep Pompey
legacy: Founded 1994 as a purification technology specialist; expanded into fermentation CDMO services through acquisitions.
notes: Specialises in chromatography purification combined with fermentation.

name: KBI Biopharma Durham
legacy: Founded 2013; acquired by JSR Corporation (Japan) in 2020. Known for fast-track development timelines.
notes: Focused on speed-to-clinic for early-phase biologics.

name: Novonesis Kalundborg
capacity: One of Europe's largest industrial fermentation complexes
legacy: Novozymes founded 2000 as spin-off from Novo Nordisk. Merged with Chr. Hansen to form Novonesis in 2024. Kalundborg site operational since the 1940s.
notes: Part of the Kalundborg Symbiosis — the world's first industrial symbiosis ecosystem.

name: dsm-firmenich Delft (Biotechnology Campus)
capacity: Multiple fermentation suites at development and pilot scale
legacy: Originated as Gist-Brocades (1869), became DSM in 1998 and merged with Firmenich in 2023. The Delft Biotechnology Campus is the global R&D and development heart of the company.
notes: Birthplace of many fermentation biotechnology innovations; large strain and culture library.

name: dsm-firmenich Sisseln
capacity: Large-scale commercial fermentation for vitamins and nutritional ingredients
legacy: Site established by Hoffmann-La Roche in the 1940s for vitamin production; acquired by DSM in 2003.
notes: One of the world's largest fermentation-based vitamin production sites.

name: CJ CheilJedang BIO Incheon
capacity: Large-scale commercial fermentation for amino acids and food ingredients
legacy: CJ CheilJedang (founded 1953) is one of the world's top producers of fermentation-derived amino acids and food ingredients. The BIO division was established in the 1980s.
notes: Global leader in fermentation-derived savory and amino acid ingredients for food and feed.

name: Evonik Health Care Hanau
capacity: Commercial fermentation for amino acids and pharma excipients
legacy: Evonik's pharma ingredients heritage traces to Degussa (founded 1843). The health care business unit was formalized in 2010.
notes: Key supplier of lipid excipients used in mRNA-LNP vaccines (including COVID-19).

name: CERBIOS-PHARMA Barbengo
capacity: Up to 25,000 L fermenters; dedicated HPAPI containment
legacy: Founded 1986 as a specialty pharma manufacturer in the Ticino region of Switzerland. HPAPI and ADC capabilities added in the 2010s.
notes: Specialist in cytotoxic and high-potency compounds alongside fermentation.

name: Lonza Portsmouth (Microbial)
legacy: Originally part of Wyeth Biopharma. Acquired by Lonza in 2012 to strengthen microbial fermentation capabilities.
notes: Lonza's primary microbial fermentation site in North America.

name: Fermion Oulu
legacy: Fermion established 1970 as part of Orion Corporation. One of the Nordic region's leading API fermentation CDMOs.
notes: Nordic specialist in fermentation-derived API manufacturing.

name: Recipharm Strängnäs
legacy: Recipharm founded 1995 in Sweden; grown to one of Europe's top CDMOs through acquisitions. The Strängnäs site specialises in fermentation-based APIs.
notes: Swedish CDMO with broad fermentation API heritage.

name: BBI Biotech Berlin
capacity: Pilot fermentation and bioreactor systems up to 1,500 L
legacy: Founded 1987 as a bioreactor instrumentation company. Expanded into contract fermentation development services.
notes: Also a leading bioreactor hardware manufacturer.

name: Lonza Biologics Pearland
legacy: Source ID: 1003
notes: Lonza's Pearland, Texas facility focuses on mammalian cell culture CDMO services with single-use bioreactor technology. The site supports clinical and commercial manufacturing for biopharmaceutical customers.

name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies RTP
legacy: Fermentation capacity up to 15,000 L; major site for biosimilar and biologic manufacturing.
notes: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies (formerly SAFC/Diosynth) in RTP is a leading CDMO offering microbial fermentation and mammalian cell culture services for clinical and commercial biologics. The site has deep expertise in recombinant proteins, including E. coli and yeast fermentation.

name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies College Station
legacy: One of the largest CDMO sites in Texas; acquired by Fujifilm in 2011.
notes: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies' College Station site (formerly Kalon Biotherapeutics) specialises in large-scale mammalian cell culture CDMO services. The site supports commercial production of monoclonal antibodies and other biologic drugs.

name: AGC Biologics Boulder
legacy: Source ID: 1008
notes: AGC Biologics Boulder (formerly CMC Biologics) provides mammalian cell culture CDMO services at clinical and commercial scales. The site specialises in monoclonal antibody production and recombinant protein manufacturing with single-use and stainless-steel bioreactor systems.

name: AGC Biologics Seattle
legacy: Source ID: 1009
notes: AGC Biologics' Seattle-area (Bothell, WA) site offers mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation CDMO capabilities. The facility supports both clinical and commercial manufacturing of biologics.

name: WuXi Biologics Cranbury
legacy: Source ID: 1011
notes: WuXi Biologics' US site in Cranbury, New Jersey provides integrated CDMO services for biologic drug development and manufacturing, including cell line development, process development, and clinical-stage production of mammalian cell culture-derived biologics.

name: Emergent BioSolutions Baltimore
legacy: Temporary FDA suspension in 2021 following contamination incident during COVID vaccine production.
notes: Emergent BioSolutions' Baltimore manufacturing site is focused on large-scale biological manufacturing for government stockpile and commercial customers. The site produces anthrax vaccines, antitoxins, and has supported COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing (AstraZeneca, J&J).

name: National Resilience Durham
legacy: Multiple NA sites including San Diego CA, Mississauga ON (Canada), Alachua FL; founded 2020 with >$2B investment.
notes: National Resilience is a CDMO with multiple North American sites. The company focuses on advanced manufacturing of biologics, gene therapies, and complex drug products, emphasising resilient domestic biomanufacturing capacity.

name: Cytovance Biologics Oklahoma City
legacy: Source ID: 1015
notes: Cytovance Biologics is a full-service biologics CDMO offering both mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation manufacturing. The site supports early-phase clinical programs and has capabilities for mAbs, recombinant proteins, and plasmid DNA production.

name: Genentech Oceanside
legacy: Opened in 2009; part of the Roche global network.
notes: Genentech's Oceanside facility is a large-scale mammalian cell culture manufacturing site focused on production of commercial biologic drugs. The site also handles fill-finish and packaging operations.

name: Bristol Myers Squibb Devens
legacy: Opened 2019; 90,000 sq ft; produces Opdivo, Eliquis intermediates.
notes: Bristol Myers Squibb's Devens biomanufacturing site is a state-of-the-art large-scale mammalian cell culture facility producing commercial biologics. The site uses single-use bioreactor technology and is one of BMS's newest and most advanced manufacturing plants.

name: Regeneron Rensselaer
legacy: One of the most productive commercial biologic manufacturing sites in the US; capacity expansions ongoing.
notes: Regeneron's Rensselaer campus is the company's primary biomanufacturing site for commercial production of its biologics portfolio including Eylea, Dupixent, Kevzara, and COVID-19 antibody therapies. The campus features large-scale mammalian cell culture manufacturing and fill-finish capabilities.

name: Biogen Research Triangle Park
legacy: Source ID: 2007
notes: Biogen's RTP facility is a large-scale mammalian cell culture manufacturing site for commercial biologics including multiple sclerosis drugs and spinal muscular atrophy therapy Spinraza. The site has been a major production hub since the 1990s.

name: AbbVie Worcester
legacy: Source ID: 2008
notes: AbbVie's Worcester site (formerly Pharmacyclics/ImmunoGen) is a biologics manufacturing facility focused on antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) production and mammalian cell culture. The site supports commercial production of oncology biologics.

name: Pfizer Andover
legacy: Site previously associated with former Wyeth biologics division.
notes: Pfizer's Andover site is one of the company's key US biomanufacturing facilities, producing commercial biologics including biosimilars and novel biologic drugs via mammalian cell culture. The site hosts significant process development and scale-up activities.

name: Pfizer McPherson
legacy: One of the world's largest COVID-19 vaccine fill-finish sites.
notes: Pfizer McPherson is a large sterile manufacturing and fill-finish facility that also handles biologics production. The site played a key role in COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing and supports commercial biologics including BioNTech mRNA COVID vaccine fill-finish.

name: Sanofi Framingham
legacy: Formerly Genzyme Framingham site prior to Sanofi acquisition.
notes: Sanofi's Framingham site is a significant biomanufacturing campus for mammalian cell culture production of commercial biologics. The site produces drugs including Dupixent (in partnership with Regeneron) and insulin products.

name: Novo Nordisk Durham
legacy: Source ID: 2012
notes: Novo Nordisk's Durham facility is a large-scale mammalian cell culture manufacturing site producing commercial biologics. Following acquisition of Catalent Bloomington, Novo Nordisk expanded US manufacturing footprint to meet growing demand for GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy.

name: Eli Lilly Indianapolis
legacy: Lilly investing >$9 billion in new US manufacturing for GLP-1 drugs as of 2023-2024.
notes: Eli Lilly's Indianapolis headquarters includes extensive biomanufacturing infrastructure for insulin, antibody, and peptide production. The site produces commercial biologics including Humalog insulin and novel GLP-1 receptor agonists (Mounjaro/tirzepatide).

name: Merck & Co. West Point
legacy: One of the largest pharmaceutical manufacturing campuses in North America.
notes: Merck's West Point campus is the company's largest US manufacturing site and global headquarters for vaccine and biologic production. The site produces multiple vaccines including Gardasil, Varivax, M-M-R II, and Pneumovax, as well as biologics such as Keytruda.

name: AstraZeneca Gaithersburg
legacy: Former MedImmune HQ; acquired by AstraZeneca in 2007.
notes: AstraZeneca's Gaithersburg site (formerly MedImmune) is a key biologics manufacturing and R&D campus. The site produces commercial vaccines and monoclonal antibodies including Synagis and Bevespi, and houses significant biologic drug development capabilities.

name: CSL Behring Kankakee
legacy: Processes millions of litres of human plasma per year.
notes: CSL Behring's Kankakee facility is a major US plasma protein fractionation and purification plant producing clotting factors, immunoglobulins (IVIG), albumin, and other plasma-derived therapeutics.

name: Grifols Los Angeles
legacy: Grifols acquired the site through the Alpha Therapeutic acquisition in 2003.
notes: Grifols' Los Angeles facility (formerly Alpha Therapeutic) is a plasma fractionation plant producing albumin, IVIG, alpha-1 antitrypsin, and clotting factors. It is one of the company's key US manufacturing sites for plasma-derived therapies.

name: Takeda Cambridge
legacy: Formerly Shire Pharmaceuticals; acquired by Takeda in 2019.
notes: Takeda's Cambridge site houses biologic drug development and early-stage manufacturing capabilities, focusing on oncology and rare disease programs. The site is a hub for cell therapy and plasma-derived biologics development.

name: Bayer Biologicals Berkeley
legacy: Historic site; in operation since 1960s for plasma biologics.
notes: Bayer's Berkeley biologicals site (formerly Miles Laboratories, then Cutter Biologicals) is one of the oldest US biologics manufacturing sites, producing plasma-derived clotting factors and recombinant hemophilia treatments including Kogenate.

name: Gilead Sciences Foster City
legacy: Kite Pharma (Gilead subsidiary) primary CAR-T manufacturing hub.
notes: Gilead Sciences' Foster City headquarters includes pharmaceutical and biologic manufacturing capabilities for antiviral and oncology products. The site manufactures CAR-T cell therapies (Yescarta and Tecartus) for commercial distribution.

name: Resilience Mississauga
legacy: Acquired from Therapure Biopharma.
notes: Resilience's Mississauga facility is a Canadian biologics manufacturing site providing CDMO services for mammalian cell culture and fill-finish operations. The site serves clinical and commercial stage customers.

name: Sanofi Connaught Campus
legacy: Connaught Laboratories founded in 1914; acquired by Sanofi (via Pasteur Mérieux) in 1989.
notes: Sanofi's Toronto Connaught campus is a historic Canadian vaccine and biologics manufacturing site, producing influenza vaccines, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis vaccines, and other biologic products. The site was built on the legacy of Connaught Laboratories, one of the world's oldest vaccine manufacturers.

name: Precision BioSciences Durham
legacy: Source ID: 3003
notes: Precision BioSciences is a genome editing company operating pilot and clinical manufacturing for allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies and in vivo gene editing products. Their Durham facility uses ARCUS nuclease technology for cell and gene therapy manufacturing.

name: Ology Biosciences Frederick
legacy: Source ID: 3004
notes: Ology Biosciences (formerly Emergent BioSolutions BARDA partner) in Frederick, Maryland operates a government-oriented biologics manufacturing facility specialising in vaccines, anthrax countermeasures, and emerging infectious disease preparedness.

name: LanzaTech Skokie
legacy: Commercial plants operating in partnership with ArcelorMittal (Belgium) and others; Skokie is the technology development hub.
notes: LanzaTech develops gas fermentation technology to convert industrial waste gases (CO, CO2) into ethanol and other chemicals. The Skokie headquarters hosts R&D and pilot-scale fermentation reactors. LanzaTech's proprietary microorganism (Clostridium autoethanogenum) is the basis of its commercial gas fermentation process.

name: Ginkgo Bioworks Boston
legacy: Went public via SPAC in 2021; operates 'Foundry' model for cell program development.
notes: Ginkgo Bioworks operates a large automated foundry for cell program design and fermentation scale-up. Their Boston facility uses synthetic biology and high-throughput automation to develop and optimise microbial and mammalian cell culture processes for industrial and pharmaceutical customers.

name: NREL Integrated Biorefinery
legacy: DOE national laboratory; open access for collaborative R&D with industry.
notes: The National Renewable Energy Laboratory's Integrated Biorefinery Research Facility (IBRF) in Golden, Colorado provides pilot- and demonstration-scale fermentation and biorefinery process development. The facility supports development of cellulosic ethanol, biofuels, and bio-based chemicals from lignocellulosic feedstocks.

name: Joint BioEnergy Institute (JBEI)
legacy: DOE-funded research institute; established 2007.
notes: The Joint BioEnergy Institute (JBEI) is a DOE Bioenergy Research Center operated by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. The Emeryville facility houses pilot-scale fermentation, synthetic biology, and biomass deconstruction research for advanced biofuels and bio-based chemicals.

name: BioMADE Ames
legacy: DOD Manufacturing USA institute; established 2020 with $87M initial award.
notes: BioMADE (Bioindustrial Manufacturing and Design Ecosystem) is a DOD-funded Manufacturing Innovation Institute. The Ames facility focuses on scale-up of industrial biomanufacturing from pilot to demonstration scale, supporting the bioeconomy through shared infrastructure and tech transition for fermentation-based chemicals, materials, and biologics.

name: Genomatica San Diego
legacy: Commercial bio-BDO production at Novamont (Italy) and BASF (Germany) under license.
notes: Genomatica develops bio-based processes for chemicals manufacturing, using engineered microorganisms. Their San Diego R&D campus houses fermentation pilot facilities for bio-butanediol (bio-BDO), bio-nylon intermediates, and other bio-based chemicals. Commercial production is licensed to partners.

name: Novozymes Blair
legacy: Major US hub for Novozymes' industrial enzyme business.
notes: Novozymes' Blair, Nebraska facility is one of the company's largest fermentation production sites for industrial enzymes. The site produces microbially fermented enzymes for ethanol, biofuels, food & beverage, and cleaning applications at industrial scale.

name: DSM-Firmenich Belvidere
legacy: One of the world's largest vitamin B12 production sites.
notes: DSM-Firmenich's Belvidere site is a large-scale fermentation and chemical synthesis facility producing vitamins (including B12), nutritional ingredients, and specialty chemicals via microbial fermentation. The site uses proprietary Pseudomonas and other microbial platforms.

name: NIIMBL University of Delaware
legacy: DOC Manufacturing USA institute; $70M federal funding since 2017.
notes: The National Institute for Innovation in Manufacturing Biopharmaceuticals (NIIMBL) is a Manufacturing USA institute headquartered at the University of Delaware. NIIMBL connects industry, academia, and government to accelerate US biopharmaceutical manufacturing innovation, including shared pilot-scale facilities and workforce development programs.

name: MIT Koch Institute Pilot Plant
legacy: Source ID: 5002
notes: MIT's Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research operates pilot-scale biomanufacturing facilities for cell therapy, mRNA, and nanoparticle drug delivery systems. The institute bridges academic research and clinical manufacturing with cGMP-compatible pilot suites.

name: BTEC North Carolina State University
legacy: One of the premier biomanufacturing education and pilot facilities in the US.
notes: The Biomanufacturing Training and Education Center (BTEC) at NC State University is a world-class facility for biomanufacturing training, pilot-scale process development, and technology scale-up. The facility operates cGMP-compatible mammalian and microbial manufacturing suites for academic and industry partners.

name: Center for Breakthrough Medicines King of Prussia
owner: Center for Breakthrough Medicines King of Prussia
legacy: 800,000+ sq ft campus; among the largest gene therapy CDMOs globally.
notes: The Center for Breakthrough Medicines (CBM) is one of the world's largest cell and gene therapy CDMOs. The King of Prussia campus provides integrated viral vector, cell therapy, and plasmid DNA manufacturing services, supporting clinical and commercial programs.

name: Forge Biologics Columbus
legacy: Founded 2020; raised over $100M Series B.
notes: Forge Biologics is a gene therapy CDMO focused exclusively on AAV manufacturing for rare disease and other gene therapy programs. The Columbus facility ('The Hearth') provides clinical and commercial-scale AAV production.

name: Andelyn Biosciences Columbus
legacy: Spun out of Nationwide Children's Hospital Research Institute in 2021.
notes: Andelyn Biosciences (formerly Nationwide Children's Hospital gene therapy CDMO) is a leading viral vector CDMO with deep expertise in AAV manufacturing for rare and inherited disease gene therapies. The Columbus facility provides GMP-grade viral vector production.

name: Wyeth Pearl River (closed)
legacy: Status: Partially closed after Pfizer acquisition 2009; some operations transferred to Pfizer sites. Wyeth founded 1926. [CLOSED]
notes: Wyeth's Pearl River facility was one of the most historic US biologics manufacturing sites, producing vaccines (Prevnar, meningococcal) and biologic drugs via mammalian cell culture. Following Pfizer's acquisition of Wyeth in 2009, the Pearl River site was restructured with parts closed and others integrated into the Pfizer network.

name: Immunex Seattle (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed; acquired by Amgen in 2002 for $16B. Manufacturing moved to Amgen West Greenwich RI. [CLOSED]
notes: Immunex Corporation was a pioneer US biotechnology company that developed Enbrel (etanercept) for rheumatoid arthritis. Immunex's Seattle manufacturing site produced Enbrel via CHO mammalian cell culture before the company was acquired by Amgen in 2002. The Seattle R&D and manufacturing operations were subsequently consolidated into Amgen's network.

name: Biogen Hilliard (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed; sold ~2015. Site now used for other purposes. [CLOSED]
notes: Biogen's Hilliard, Ohio biomanufacturing facility was built in the early 2000s as additional capacity for interferon beta production (Avonex). The site was decommissioned and sold as Biogen restructured its manufacturing network and consolidated production.

name: Diosynth RTP (closed / acquired)
legacy: Status: Acquired and rebranded as Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies RTP (see entry 1004). [CLOSED]
notes: Diosynth Biotechnologies RTP was an early CDMO offering microbial and mammalian manufacturing services. Diosynth (formerly Akzo Nobel Diosynth) was acquired by SAFC (Sigma-Aldrich) and subsequently by Fujifilm in 2011 to form Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies. The RTP site continued operating under Fujifilm ownership.

name: Genzyme Allston (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed post-Sanofi acquisition; manufacturing consolidated to other Sanofi/Genzyme sites. The 2009 Allston Vesivirus contamination is a landmark case study in biomanufacturing risk. [CLOSED]
notes: Genzyme's Allston facility was the primary manufacturing site for the rare disease enzyme replacement therapies including Cerezyme (imiglucerase) for Gaucher disease. A 2009 contamination incident caused a global shortage and patient crisis. The site was subsequently modernised. Sanofi acquired Genzyme in 2011.

name: Amgen Seattle (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed; Amgen Seattle R&D retained but manufacturing consolidated. Site vacated ~2018. [CLOSED]
notes: Amgen operated a manufacturing and R&D site in Seattle following its acquisition of Immunex in 2002. This site (formerly Immunex) was gradually consolidated as Amgen centralised biologics production to its West Greenwich and Thousand Oaks sites. The Seattle facility was primarily R&D-focused in its later years.

name: Covance Biologics Mooresville (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed ~2016 after LabCorp acquisition of Covance. [CLOSED]
notes: Covance Biologics operated a mammalian cell culture CDMO site in Mooresville, NC focused on clinical-stage biologics manufacturing. The site was closed following LabCorp's acquisition of Covance in 2015 and subsequent restructuring. Previously served clinical development customers with GMP mAb production.

name: Albany Molecular Research (AMRI) Albany (closed)
legacy: Status: Company split after Bridgepoint acquisition 2017; Albany biologics operations closed. [CLOSED]
notes: Albany Molecular Research Inc (AMRI) operated CRO/CDMO services from its Albany headquarters with biologics capabilities. AMRI was acquired by Bridgepoint in 2017 and subsequently split into multiple entities. The biologics manufacturing assets were absorbed or closed.

name: Charles River Biologics Bloomington
legacy: Source ID: 1016
notes: Charles River Laboratories offers biologics testing, cell banking, and early-phase CDMO services at multiple US sites. Their biologics operations support cell line characterisation, master/working cell bank production, and viral safety testing for pharmaceutical clients.

name: Phibro Animal Health Teaneck
legacy: Source ID: 1017
notes: Phibro Animal Health manufactures vaccines and biologics for animal health applications. US sites produce fermentation-based veterinary vaccines and pharmaceutical products using both mammalian cell culture and microbial fermentation.

name: Patheon/Thermo Fisher Biologics Brisbane
legacy: Patheon acquired by Thermo Fisher for $7.2B in 2017.
notes: Thermo Fisher Scientific (via Patheon acquisition) operates biologics CDMO services from multiple North American sites. The Emeryville, CA site offers mammalian cell culture process development and clinical manufacturing for biopharmaceutical customers.

name: Samsung Biologics America San Francisco
legacy: Manufacturing primarily in Incheon, Korea; US office supports North American customers.
notes: Samsung Biologics maintains a North American presence through its San Francisco business development office and CDO (Contract Development Organization) services. While primary manufacturing is in Incheon, Korea, the company actively pursues US partnerships and has announced plans for US-based manufacturing.

name: ElevateBio Waltham
legacy: Founded 2017; raised $850M+. BaseCamp is a 150,000 sq ft facility.
notes: ElevateBio is a technology and manufacturing company for cell and gene therapies. Their Waltham, MA facility ('BaseCamp') provides integrated viral vector and cell therapy manufacturing capabilities, combining process development and GMP production for multiple gene therapy programs.

name: Vigene Biosciences Rockville
legacy: Source ID: 1021
notes: Vigene Biosciences is a viral vector CDMO providing AAV, lentivirus, adenovirus, and retrovirus manufacturing for gene therapy research and clinical programs. The Rockville facility offers both GMP and non-GMP viral vector production.

name: Waisman Biomanufacturing Madison
legacy: Academic CDMO; focuses on under-resourced developers who cannot access commercial CDMOs.
notes: Waisman Biomanufacturing at the University of Wisconsin-Madison is an academic CDMO that provides GMP-grade manufacturing of biologics, cell therapies, and viral vectors for clinical trials. The facility supports early-phase IND-enabling manufacturing for academic and small biotech customers.

name: Protein Design Labs (PDL) BioPharma Fremont (closed)
legacy: Status: Closed; PDL BioPharma dissolved in 2020. [CLOSED]
notes: Protein Design Labs was a pioneering antibody humanisation company that operated manufacturing and R&D at Fremont, CA. The company later became PDL BioPharma and focused on its patent royalty business rather than manufacturing. The Fremont R&D and pilot manufacturing facility was wound down.

name: AstraZeneca Frederick
legacy: Source ID: 2021
notes: AstraZeneca operates a biologics manufacturing facility at its Maryland campus that supports commercial production of respiratory and oncology biologics. The site was significantly involved in COVID-19 vaccine manufacturing (AZD1222) via subcontracting with Emergent BioSolutions.

name: Sanofi Swiftwater
legacy: Formerly Wyeth-Lederle (then Aventis Pasteur) site; one of the oldest US vaccine facilities in continuous operation.
notes: Sanofi's Swiftwater facility is one of the world's largest influenza vaccine manufacturing sites, producing hundreds of millions of influenza vaccine doses annually via egg-based and cell-based processes. The site also manufactures rabies and other vaccines.

name: Archer Daniels Midland Decatur
legacy: One of the largest bioprocessing complexes in the world by volume.
notes: ADM's Decatur campus includes large-scale wet mill corn processing and fermentation for ethanol, lysine, citric acid, sorbitol, and other bio-based chemicals. The site is one of the largest corn wet mills in North America and represents industrial-scale fermentation and bioproduction.

name: Cargill Blair Fermentation
legacy: Source ID: 4010
notes: Cargill operates large-scale fermentation facilities for food ingredients, amino acids, and industrial biochemicals at its Blair, NE site. The facility produces lysine and other amino acids via microbial fermentation for feed and food markets.

name: Sanofi Genzyme Waltham
legacy: Formerly Genzyme Corp; acquired by Sanofi for $20.1B in 2011.
notes: Sanofi's Genzyme campus in Cambridge/Waltham is a major biologics manufacturing and R&D hub producing rare disease enzyme replacement therapies including Cerezyme, Fabrazyme, Aldurazyme, and Myozyme. These complex lysosomal storage disease therapies are produced via mammalian cell culture.

name: Intrexon Germantown (closed)
legacy: Status: Rebranded as Precigen; Germantown manufacturing activities reduced after business restructuring 2020. [CLOSED]
notes: Intrexon (now Precigen) operated synthetic biology and biomanufacturing facilities in Germantown, MD. The site hosted development of UltraVector synthetic biology platform and pilot-scale fermentation for engineered microorganisms producing biofuels, health products, and other bio-based chemicals.

name: Meihua Holdings Group Co. Ltd
legacy: Listed on Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Largest single-site amino acid fermentation complex in the world.
notes: World's largest amino acid producer, specialising in glutamic acid, lysine, threonine, valine and other feed and food amino acids via large-scale microbial fermentation from corn feedstocks. Annual capacity exceeds 1.5 million tonnes of amino acid products across 6 production bases in China.

name: Fufeng Group Co. Ltd

owner: Lesaffre – Tianjin Lesaffre Yeast Co. Ltd

name: Henan Jindan Lactic Acid Technology Co. Ltd
owner: Henan Jindan Lactic Acid Technology Co. Ltd

owner: Novozymes (China) Investment Co. Ltd – Tianjin Plant

name: Habio Bioengineering Co. Ltd

name: Shandong Longlive Bio-Technology Co. Ltd

name: Jilin Roquette Starch Co. Ltd

Capacity ~400,000 tonnes corn processed per year.

name: DSM Nutritional Products (China) Ltd – Tianjin

owner: Tsingtao Brewery Co. Ltd – Qingdao Main Plant

name: Qingdao Seawin Biotech Group Co. Ltd
owner: Qingdao Seawin Biotech Group Co. Ltd

name: Bluepha Co. Ltd

notes: Biotechnology startup pioneering continuous non-sterile PHA (polyhydroxyalkanoate) bioplastic production. name: Shenzhen Ecomann Biotechnology Co. Ltd

name: Guangdong VTR Bio-Tech Co. Ltd

notes: Industrial microbiology contract manufacturer in Guangdong Province. Works with international agrochemical and food ingredient companies on scale-up projects.

name: Jiangnan University – Nat. Engineering Research Center for Cereal Fermentation

China's leading academic fermentation science institution with strong industry partnerships (Angel Yeast, Meihua, etc.).

name: Shanghai Institute of Plant Physiology & Ecology (SIPPE), CAS

name: Ajinomoto Co. Inc. – Tokai Plant

name: Korea Research Institute of Bioscience & Biotechnology (KRIBB)

name: dsm-firmenich Leeuwarden

name: Novonesis Hørsholm – Food Cultures & Probiotics Campus

notes: Novonesis group headquarters and primary food culture & probiotic production facility in Hørsholm, Denmark. Inherits Chr. Hansen's 150-year history of microbial culture science. Produces direct-vat-set (DVS) dairy cultures, probiotic strains (incl. BB-12® Bifidobacterium and LGG®-equivalent strains), plant-based fermentation cultures and bioprotective cultures for food safety. Houses the world's largest collection of lactic acid bacteria (~50,000 strains) and the global Novonesis R&D and innovation centre.

name: Novonesis Franklinton
